shortDescription: Stacks up to 7 playable z-levels (3 up / 3 down) into ONE banded RimWorld Map joined by synthetic RegionLink wormholes, so hauling, needs, work and storage come free from vanilla. Four vanilla-matched per-level sizes (126/190/250/300) and level counts are bought from a fixed 192,000-cell budget. Per-colony climate bands make high levels genuinely alpine. Mountain mass renders through every level down to the first solid floor, which is what makes a deep column read as depth.
body:
> **NOTE TO SELF:** running spec, not a changelog. §0 handover; §1-19 architecture; §20 compat; §21-29 bug records. Keep every ⚠ - each cost a run to learn.

# As above, So below II (V2)

> V1 is DELETED. ~72 files, ~21,000 LOC. No em-dashes anywhere in shipped text.

# 0. START HERE (handover, end of the renderer session)

**What this mod is.** Up to seven z-levels in ONE RimWorld `Map`, banded along +z. Priorities in order: (1) visual clarity from above, (2) performance, (3) vanilla parity.

**Where the work just was.** A five-bug chain in the below-view mass renderer (§24b, §24c, §27, §28/§28b, §29), all reported from screenshots. **The user has now called visuality done: "good as its going to get".** Do not reopen the mass renderer for polish - reopen it only on a new report.

**State of the renderer toggles**, all in `SectionLayer_ABMountainCap`, all in the bisect stamp:
| toggle | default | debug action | status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CornerFillersEnabled` | on | AB: toggle cap corner fillers | verified |
| `MassFieldFadeEnabled` | on | AB2: toggle mass field fade | **verified in play (§28)** |
| `MassDepthCutEnabled` | **on** | AB2: toggle mass depth cut | **accepted on LOOK only (#260); FRAME COST NEVER MEASURED** |

**The single most important open risk.** §29's depth cut ships ON having been judged only by eye. It emits up to one fill + one outline **per level** per column over deep mass, and §10-12 says the cost of this mod lives in section-regeneration BURSTS, not steady-state fps - which is exactly what this multiplies. **If any performance report arrives on a mountainous map, throw that switch first.** Flipping the default back is the entire fix.

**How to test anything here.** `run_test_cycle`, then read the profile's TILE line BEFORE looking at pixels - three test runs were wasted on tiles that could not express the bug (§9c-9f). For mass rendering you need `hilliness Mountainous`; for snow you need sub-zero; for queue-ordering you need two or more stone types in the SUPPRESSED census.

---

## Status
Visuality, QOL, altitude/weather, settings VERIFIED. **250 tier VERIFIED (#236); 190x5 VERIFIED (#237-#240).**
**✅ §24b (#240, with BM) ✅ §24c (#248, vanilla) ✅ §27 (below-snow fade) ✅ §28 (eroded fill) ✅ §29 accepted on look (#260).**
**🔧 §25 FIXED, UNVERIFIED** (fog-on-reload + doubled/inverted stairs, one `ABSkySync` bug + repair sweep). **This is the biggest untested thing in the mod and it needs the reporter's save.**
UNVERIFIED: §25, §29 cost, depth shrink, camera anchor, §18 audit, reroll grid, VEE compat, GL roof fix.

**PUBLISHED-BUILD BUGS.** 1. Preview 190-only - FIXED (§6d-CLAMP). 2. Fog/rocks on reload - FIXED (§25). 3. GL rivers - TABLED (§22). 4. MO formations 4x overlapping - FIXED (§24a). 5. Rock only one level down - FIXED+VERIFIED (§24b). 6. Stairs invert/double on reload - FIXED (§25). 7. Rounded-corner holes, non-BM only - FIXED+VERIFIED (§24c). 8. Below-snow fade inverted - FIXED+VERIFIED (§27). 9. Square fill past the mass outline - FIXED+VERIFIED (§28). 10. Red rim on eroded edges - FIXED (§28b). 11. Tiers stacked not continuous - FIXED (§29).

---

# 1. ARCHITECTURE
One `Map`, size `(w, 1, bandCount * Slot)`. Bands stack along +z from the deepest basement, gutter between. `Slot = ceil((bandHeight + MinGutter)/64)*64`; **64-alignment of SLOT is load-bearing** (terrain shaders sample by world position).

**The one insight.** `Region.Neighbors` is *topological, not spatial*. Wormhole `RegionLink`s between one-cell `RegionType.Portal` ends conduct connectivity without merging rooms, temperature or vacuum, and `Reachability.CanReach` works unpatched. But reachability is not a path: 1.6's pathfinder is jobified and cannot traverse a synthetic link, hence segmented movement (§3).

**Hard 1.6 constraints.** Path grid is IJobParallelFor over EVERY cell, so total stacked cells is the runtime metric. No `PathFinder.FindPath`. `BlocksDiagonalMovement` trips on unwalkable cells.

**⚠ The stack is 2x to 7x anisotropic.** Anything vanilla normalises by BOTH dimensions is distorted - a bug class that cannot appear on a square map.

### ⚠ THE SLICING RULE, seven shapes
| Shape | Example | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Anchor, a fraction of `Size.z` | river/lake centre; random/edge cell; VEE Crater jitter | remap the point |
| Field, a gradient on map centre | coastline (§6e); VEE LoneIsland and Crater | re-centre the sample coordinate |
| Noise space, a slice is not a short map | Map Preview (§6d); GL landform grids (§22) | generate at full height, then crop |
| Distance-to-extent, a margin off `Size` | `CloseToEdge`, no-build edge; river WIDTH | re-base onto the cell's band rect |
| **Aspect ratio, normalised by BOTH dims** | preview window and reroll grid (§6d) | lay out from the BAND, generate at the STACK |
| **Map-wide scalar** | snow melt (§7), temperature readout (§16), GL roof sweep | rewrite it per cell at the consumer |
| **Foreign absolute writes** (§22) | GL landform output lands in band 0, our carve overwrites it | ORDER, not arithmetic |

Still unaudited: Basin, Cavern, Chasm, Cliffs, Hollow, Valley (all `FalloffAtAngle`).
**`ABBandLocal.cs` is THE canonical FIELD rewrite** plus `BandLocalModule`, a `ModuleBase` wrapper for direct noise samplers.

# 2. LEVEL PLAN, budget 192,000 cells
**⚠ THE 64 CONSTRAINT IS ON *SLOT*, NOT BAND HEIGHT.** The original tiers were all 64k-2 and **that coincidence was mistaken for the requirement for months**.

| size | slot | gutter | cells/band | playable | max levels | total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 126 | 128 | 2 | 16,128 | 98.4% | 7 (cap) | 112,896 |
| 190 | 192 | 2 | 36,480 | 99.0% | 5 | 182,400 ✅ |
| **250** | 256 | 6 | 64,000 | 97.7% | 3 | **192,000** ✅ |
| **300** | 320 | 20 | 96,000 | 93.8% | 2 | **192,000** |

250/300 are vanilla's Medium and Large exactly. **Budget is tuned:** 192,000 = `3 x 64,000` = `2 x 96,000`. Ladder 7/5/3/2.
**⚠ 200 IS THE ONE NUMBER TO AVOID** - slot 256, gutter 56, 21.9% wasted. **Waste is a SAWTOOTH.**
**⚠ A WIDE GUTTER IS A FEATURE** - "a spatial helper that reaches 22 rows will cross a 2-row gutter" is the root of §15a and §4.
**Old saves are safe** - `bandHeight` is scribed; `SlotFor` is generic. **`Size.x == bandHeight` is a repair tool.**
**⚠ THE PLAN PERSISTS BETWEEN COLONIES AND SILENTLY CONSTRAINS THE SIZE.** Read the PLAN line before believing any size test.
**⚠ Own the widget, do not patch the data.** Our radio buttons write `GameInitData.mapSize` directly. **Adding a tier means growing the `InitialSize` postfix** (now +288f). **The chooser LATCHES global state, released in a `Finalizer`.**

# 3-5. MOVEMENT, ORDERING, DESCENT
**Cross-band movement** segmented at ONE interception; hops must strictly decrease. **Multi-hop UNTESTED IN PLAY.**
**Group ordering:** the drag line between bands runs through the GUTTER; the odd/even signature ("3 and 5 fail, 2 and 4 do not") is the proof - only ODD counts sample exactly 0.5.
**⚠ ONE DESCENT RULE: `TryResolveVisibleBelow`.** TEN systems share it. **NINE appearances of the single-step bug** - eight as `- Slot` arithmetic, **the ninth (§24b) as a TERRAIN-DEF GATE with no arithmetic in it at all**. **`TryResolveVisibleFrom` is THE gate.**
**⚠ AND THE GATE ANSWERS TWO QUESTIONS, NOT ONE** (§27): *which* level a cell shows, and *whether* it shows anything.
**⚠ §29 ADDS A SECOND, RENDERING-ONLY DESCENT BESIDE IT - NOT A WIDENING OF IT.** `BuildDepthStack` treats mass as translucent, which is true of how mass is DRAWN and false of everything else about it. Widening the shared rule would make rock reachable, clickable and shootable through three levels. **It is a different question asked beside the rule, never a copy of it.**

# 6. SKY-MASS PRESENTATION
Despeckle (walls dissolve only at 7+ open neighbours; at 6 it ate the outermost wall row off every meadow edge), central fog hole, five-terrain plateau palette, cliff faces, alpine pass.
**⚠ The mass tapers with altitude, so +3 may contain NO LAND AT ALL.** Quantified (#237): surface 12,723 plants / fertility 0.631; +1 248 / 0.069; +2 170 / 0.046; +3 **37 / 0.012**.
**⚠ THE SKY BAND'S OWN MASS IS `AB_MountainTop` TERRAIN AND NOTHING ELSE IDENTIFIES IT.** `ABSkyBandGen` writes it for `KindLedge` (no edifice, no roof) and `KindWall` (rock edifice + `RoofRockThick`). Hence `ABSkySync` may only create `AB_MountainTop`, never overwrite one (§25).
**Snow-holding decides where snow fades:** `AB_OpenAir`/`AB_WallTop` are `holdSnowOrSand=false`; **`AB_MountainTop` and `AB_RoofSurface` hold snow.** A `KindWall` cell stays bare because its rock edifice is Full fillage and `SnowGrid.CanHaveSnow` rejects it. So vanilla's snow layer fades correctly on a sky band unaided - which proved §27 was ours.

# 6a. ⚠ THE BELOW VIEW IS MIRRORED PASSES, NOT ONE RENDERER
`SectionLayer_ABBelowV2` ports vanilla `SectionLayer_Terrain` **and nothing else**. Confirmed five times: Water (§6b), Snow (§6f), mass sprites (§24b), linked corner fillers (§24c), snow's visibility kernel (§27).
**⚠ THE CONVERSE IS HANDLED.** A foreign `Thing.Print` postfix prints into OUR layer and is still correct, because the call is bracketed `SnapshotVertCounts()` -> `Print` -> `FinishNewVerts`, and **`FinishNewVerts` transforms by VERTEX RANGE**. Preserve that.
**⚠ THREE DIFFERENT THINGS ARE ALL CALLED "MASS", AND THEY ARE REPRESENTED DIFFERENTLY** (cost three failed fixes, §24b):
| what | representation | drawn by |
|---|---|---|
| undug GROUND mountain | a real rock **edifice**, but FOGGED so its sprite is never printed | cap, from one Slot up |
| SKY-band mass | `AB_MountainTop` **terrain**, NO edifice at all | cap, into that band's own mesh |
| mined-out floor | rock leave-**terrain** | `ABMinedRockLookup` |
**Any code that tests only `edificeGrid` misses sky mass; any code that tests only terrain misses undug ground.** `CarriesMass` is the cheap yes/no for neighbour scans; `MassRockAt` also NAMES the stone.
**⚠ AND THE MASS FILL IS EMITTED FROM THREE PLACES** (§28): the cap's in-band pass, `EmitMassRepresentationAt`, and `PrintBelowTerrain`'s base quad via the `AB_MountainTop` -> host-rough-stone substitution. **Any change to how mass FILL looks must land in all three or it half-fixes and stacks.** They share `EmitFieldAt` / `MassFanCoverage` / `TryMassFillCoverage`.
**⚠ THE CAP IS SINGLE-STEP.** `SectionLayer_ABMountainCap` derives from `-bands.Slot`, exactly one band down.
**Ascent rule:** the dirty mirror stops at the first opaque floor, tested over the cell and its eight neighbours; the FIRST step stays unconditional *because* the cap is single-step.
**⚠ THE UNIT OF WASTE IS A SECTION REGENERATION, NOT A CELL.** §29 multiplies that unit by the level count on mountainous maps.
**⚠ VISIBILITY IS DECIDED ENTIRELY BY `ABBands.ShowsBelow(terrain)`, SO A TERRAIN SWAP IS A RENDERING BUG.** `AB_WallTop`/`AB_OpenAir` see-through; `AB_MountainTop`/`AB_RoofSurface` opaque. That is §25.
**⚠ A SMOOTHING KERNEL IS A SECOND CONSUMER OF THAT SAME RULE** (§27). Any mirrored pass that averages over neighbours must apply `ShowsBelow` to every sample, not only to the cell it is colouring.
**⚠ AND A `dontRender` VIEWING CELL MEANS OUR FILL IS THE ONLY BACKDROP** (§28b). Vanilla's terrain layer emits only a ShadowMask there, so ANY transparency we introduce exposes shader garbage - a saturated red/magenta rim. Every alpha-blended thing drawn into an open-air column needs a guaranteed opaque layer beneath it, and §29 now proves that guarantee with a measured `laidOpaque` flag rather than asserting it.

# 6b-6g. WATER, PREVIEW, COASTS, SNOW, SHRINK
**Water** is TWO-PASS SCREEN-SPACE; `SectionLayer_ABBelowWatergen` targets `SubcameraDefOf.WaterDepth.LayerId`. Rivers remap `GetRiverCenter` (not `Init`); `GetLakeCenter` needs the same. Width clamped at the producer. **⚠ ALL THREE INERT UNDER GL** (§22).
**⚠ 6d-CLAMP:** `Stacked()` ran the incoming size through `Clamp()`, which returns *the largest offered size ≤ input that fits*; Map Preview passes VANILLA's size, so `Clamp(250)` returned 190 **regardless of the player's pick**. **Fix: `PlannedSize`.**
**⚠ MAP PREVIEW SHIPS IN TWO HALVES AND GL BUNDLES ONE.** With GL installed and Map Preview absent, `Active` is TRUE while window types are ABSENT. **Do not "simplify" `Active`.**
**6d-REROLL:** the window opened EMPTY - `elementSize.y = 403/126*896 = 2,866 px` -> `gridSize.y = 0` -> `DesiredCount = 0`.
**Coasts:** CENTRED wrong, not scaled wrong. NO SCALING. **⚠ "None override `GetNoiseValue`" is about VANILLA ONLY.**
**6f. Below-snow:** geometry built ONCE, only colours rewritten - **never `ClearSubMeshes(All)` here**. Every cell must emit exactly nine colours including invisible ones, or all later cells shift onto the wrong vertices.
**Depth shrink (UNVERIFIED):** **⚠ the atlas trap** - past `ZoomRootSize` 18 humanlikes render from a cached atlas blit ignoring `PawnDrawParms.matrix`. **⚠ natural rock excluded BY DEF, not by link type** (`mineable || isNaturalRock`), because BM makes rock non-linked. That exclusion also killed the "inset outline = shrunken sprite" theory in §28b - **check it before blaming shrink for any size mismatch.**
**⚠ PERSPECTIVE MODE WAS BUILT AND REMOVED. Do not re-add as polish.**

# 7-8a. CHARACTER, CAMERA
Ore `x(1+0.45*(depth-1))` scales `basementOreDensity` through our OWN `ABOreGen.ScatterOres`. **⚠ The snow line never worked, and the comment saying it did not need to was wrong.**
**The camera clamp and level-switch input share `ABGuard.Camera`**, both per-frame paths where an unthrottled `Log.Error` turns a cosmetic bug into a hang.
**New-game anchor:** only `StartedNewGame` runs after vanilla's own camera jump. ⚠ OPEN: `z=24` was EXACTLY `PodScatterMargin`.

# 9. GENERATION COST

## 9a. The profile stamps its own conditions
Prints `TILE`, `PLAN`, `SCOPING:`, two censuses, and now the bisect state. Has voided or explained EIGHT comparisons. **⚠ THE WATER REPORT DOES NOT AND SHOULD.**

## 9b. ⚠ "COST IS DESTRUCTION NOT GENERATION" - NO LONGER TRUE, AND THE FIX IS WHY
#188 was 16/84. #231 is 71/29. Rock suppression worked, so the carve got cheap and cost moved to generation. **A historical record of a fixed problem.**

## 9c-9f. Measured cost curve, twelve tiles
| run | plan | tile | gensteps | carve | total | destroyed | suppressed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| #231 | 7x126 | Flat TropSwamp | 3,836 | 1,580 | ~5.7 s | 4,575 | 1,627 |
| #236 | 3x250 | SmallHills | 5,001 | **7,118** | ~12.4 s | 15,611 | 7,272 |
| #237 | 5x190 | Mountainous | 4,529 | 2,201 | ~6.9 s | 7,497 | 85,304 |
| #238 | 5x190 | SmallHills | 3,389 | 4,718 | ~8.3 s | 16,100 | 11,175 |
| #239 | 5x190 | Mountainous Desert | 2,217 | 2,357 | **~4.7 s** | 7,906 | 76,702 |
| #248 | 5x190 | Flat Tundra | 2,108 | 3,282 | ~5.4 s | 12,103 | 5,689 |
| #254 | 5x190 | Flat Desert | 2,133 | 3,033 | ~5.2 s | 12,920 | 5,889 |
| #255 | 5x190 | Mountainous Boreal | 2,404 | **1,743** | ~4.1 s | 5,883 | **94,282** |
| #257 | 5x190 | Mountainous Boreal | 2,326 | 2,839 | ~5.2 s | 11,021 | 81,984 |
| #258 | 5x190 | Mountainous Boreal | 2,380 | 2,977 | ~5.4 s | 13,004 | 84,813 |
| #259 | 5x190 | Mtn Boreal **+Caves** | 3,375 | 1,937 | ~5.3 s | 7,113 | 87,365 |
| #260 | 5x190 | Mtn Boreal **+Caves** | 3,488 | 2,352 | ~5.8 s | 10,404 | 93,221 |

**⚠ FillRock is SUPERLINEAR in band size:** 190 -> 36,480 cells -> ~960-2,385 ms; 250 -> 64,000 cells -> 4,254 ms. **1.75x cells, 2.87x time**, as the `ListerThings` linear-`List.Remove` mechanism predicts.
**⚠ HILLINESS DECIDES THE BILL, AND THE MOUNTAINOUS EXTREME IS THE CHEAPEST.** #255 is the fastest carve on record (1,743 ms) on the most mountainous tile, versus ~3,000 ms on flat: suppressed rock is never spawned, where a hilly-but-not-mountainous map pays to spawn and then destroy.
**⚠ THE `Caves` MUTATOR COSTS ~1.1-1.2 s IN `MutatorPostElevationFertility`** (#259, #260), versus ~47 ms without it - the largest single genstep on those maps. **Vanilla's, and tile-dependent, so it does NOT jump the optimisation queue** (see the tile-independence rule below).
**⚠ AND HILLINESS ALSO DECIDES WHETHER A RENDERING TEST IS VALID AT ALL** (#248, #254). A Flat tile spawns no mass wide enough to have mask-15 interiors; a warm tile seeds no snow (`SeedAltitudeSnow` 1.3 ms on Desert 28.5C vs 6.1 ms on Boreal 0.3C); a one-stone map cannot express a queue-ordering bug. **Read the TILE and SUPPRESSED lines before reading the screenshot.**
**⚠ THE 250 TIER IS THE EXPENSIVE ONE** (~12.4 s vs ~4.1-8.3 s at 190). I recommended the 192,000 budget reasoning about PATHFINDING and did not predict generation time would double.

## 9g. ⚠ RE-RANKED ON EVIDENCE, AGAINST MY OWN EARLIER ADVICE
`GenStep_Plants` across twelve tiles: **61.5 ms to 2,270 ms**, a 37x spread dominated by rainfall.
Four successive wrong claims about this one number: *"84% is grown then erased"* (false), *"biome-independent"* (dead at n=3), *"tracks hilliness"* (dead at n=4), *"1.1-2.3 s"* (dead at n=5).
**Basement `FillRock` is 960-4,254 ms on EVERY tile.** Tile-independent beats tile-dependent, so:
1. **Basement rock suppression** - consistently ~1.0-4.3 s. **Item 1.**
2. **`GenStep_Plants` traversal scoping** - 0.06-2.3 s. **Demoted.**
3. **`GenStep_RockChunks`** - `Filth_RubbleRock` is top-3 destroyed on every tile.
4. Scattered ruins (also a CONTENT BUG). 5. Perlin precompute (changes determinism).

# 10-12. PERF AND DIAGNOSTICS
59.6 fps at 96 pawns. **⚠ THAT BENCHMARK MEASURES THE WRONG THING** - cost is in section-regeneration BURSTS, which is exactly what §29 multiplies and what has never been measured.
**⚠ Bisect toggles PERSIST across runs.** STAMPED INTO THE PROFILE, and the stamp now carries `massFieldFade` and `massDepthCut` too - **an unstamped toggle is how a later reading gets poisoned, which is why the stamp exists at all.**
**⚠ The pre-pinned palette always strips its LAST entry. n=13.** Keep padding with a DISTINCT throwaway.
**⚠ THE AUTO-PROMPT IS EDGE-TRIGGERED, SO CHECK THE COUNT, NOT THE TEXT.**
**⚠ OUR OWN PROFILE AND BISECT LINES ARRIVE AS `warning` ROWS ATTRIBUTED TO US.** Deliberate - info level is filtered out of the bridge - so a run reporting only those is a CLEAN run. Read the profile for TILE/PLAN first.
**⚠ Debug actions are `AllowedGameStates.PlayingOnMap`** - silently inert on the world map / preview screen.
**⚠ AUDIT A DIAGNOSTIC'S OWN FILTERS BEFORE TRUSTING A NEGATIVE.** The below-layer report filtered on `StartsWith("SectionLayer_ABBelow")`, excluding `SectionLayer_ABMountainCap`. **A missing row and an empty row are indistinguishable.** Now `SectionLayer_AB`.

# 13. OPEN WORK
1. **MEASURE §29's frame cost** on a mountainous map while panning. It ships ON, judged by eye only. If it stutters, flip `MassDepthCutEnabled` back to false - that is the whole fix.
2. **VERIFY §25 on the reporter's save** - fog blob gone from the sky band, stairs single, repair line in the log with a non-zero count. Biggest untested thing in the mod.
3. **Basement rock suppression** (§9g item 1).
4. Verify tiers 126/300; preview at 300; §18 audit; VEE compat; GL roof fix; reroll grid; depth shrink; camera anchor.
5. Stamp TILE/PLAN into the water report.
6. §9g items 2-5; audit the other `FalloffAtAngle` mutators.
7. **Never exercised:** multi-hop stair router, elevator, basement PATHING/wormholes, cavern basement.
8. `ShotReport` drops target size. Biomes! at 40%. Better Trees unexamined (§23c). **Store page still says three levels.**
9. **§22 TABLED** - do not resume without re-reading the contradiction.
10. **CAI 5000 fog of war is a standing save-corruption risk we do not control** (§26). Only pursue if fog persists after §25.
11. **§29 known-unmeasured:** the atlas OUTLINE tiles are not depth-queued. Same rock type is fine (one submesh, submission order settles it); two different rock types at different depths tie on queue and are undefined. Thin, never observed, deferred.

# 14. LESSONS
**Method.** Prove a subsystem innocent by finding a state where the suspect CANNOT EXIST. Re-open a rejection only by naming the confound. Change one thing per experiment. Run the diagnostic before the third theory. A beautiful fit is not evidence.
**⚠ ASSERTING AN INVARIANT IS NOT ESTABLISHING IT.** §29 shipped "the bottom entry never erodes, therefore the bottom is opaque" - a claim about the code's intent, not about the mesh. `PrintBelowTerrain` returns early and draws NOTHING on a `dontRender` or material-less cell, so everything above eroded onto a hole. Replaced by a `laidOpaque` flag carried up the stack. **If a later step depends on an earlier one having produced something, carry the ANSWER, not the assumption.**
**⚠ HALF-IMPOSED ORDERING IS WORSE THAN NONE.** §29 re-queued the deeper levels and left the nearest on its natural queue, which inverts exactly when the deep terrain out-ranks the near one (stone 190+ over soil) - and only on maps with two or more stone types, so it looks intermittent. **When you take over an ordering, take over ALL of it.**
**⚠ FIXING A HOLE BY LOOKING SIDEWAYS WHEN THE ANSWER WAS DOWNWARD.** §28b's backdrop borrowed terrain from a lateral neighbour, which made every tier read as a slab lying on the next. **When a spatial system needs "what is behind this", check the axis the system is actually about before taking the nearest thing.**
**⚠ COUNT THE EMITTERS BEFORE FIXING THE LOOK.** §28's fill came from THREE places; fixing one looks like partial success, the artifact persisting on the levels the others own. **"This appears once per level" means establish the emitter count FIRST.**
**⚠ CLEAR THE OTHER SUSPECT BY READING ITS DATA, NOT ITS CODE.** §27: one grep of our terrain defs (`holdSnowOrSand`, Full fillage) proved vanilla's kernel already sees zeroes in the right cells. **A def field can exonerate a whole layer faster than reading either layer.**
**⚠ A FIX FOR MOD X CAN BE A REGRESSION FOR EVERYONE WITHOUT X, AND THE BRANCH IS WHERE TO LOOK.** §24c: the BM fix added ONE emitter with two halves and only the BM half was exercised. **The untested branch is the one on the majority configuration.**
**⚠ REPRODUCING A SUBSYSTEM MEANS REPRODUCING ALL OF IT.** An atlas tile is HALF of `Graphic_LinkedCornerFiller` (§24c) - and the tile is only half of *vanilla rock*, because **its TRANSPARENCY is load-bearing too** (§28).
**⚠ A COMMENT THAT JUSTIFIES SKIPPING ONE CHECK CAN BE HIDING A SECOND CHECK IT NEVER MENTIONS** (§27). **When a comment defends an omission, name every question the omitted call would have answered.**
**⚠ REUSING A PREDICATE IS REUSING ITS HIDDEN CONDITIONS.** §28b: `massCell` is the DECORATION gate and carries `drop > slot`, which exists to stop two emitters double-drawing - irrelevant to a FILL, and it excluded the commonest case. **Twice in one feature. Ask what question the predicate was built to answer.**
**⚠ AN EVENT HOOK THAT LOOKS INCREMENTAL MAY BE A FULL-MAP SWEEP ON THE LOAD PATH.** `Building.SpawnSetup` calls `edificeGrid.Register` **without consulting `respawningAfterLoad`** (§25).
**⚠ TWO RESOLVERS FOR ONE QUANTITY IS A BUG WITH A DELAY FUSE** (§25). **When you add a live updater beside a generator, make one call the other or diff them line by line.**
**⚠ A FIX APPLIED TO ONE CASE MUST BE CARRIED TO ITS SIBLING, AND THE COMMENT PROVES IT WAS NOT.** `ABSkySync`'s header documented "ROOF BEATS EDIFICE" and only the constructed-roof branch was ordered that way.
**⚠ READ THE GUARD CLAUSES OF THE HELPER YOU ARE ABOUT TO REUSE - INCLUDING YOUR OWN** (§24b).
**⚠ ASK HOW THE SUBSYSTEM REPRESENTS THE THING, NOT WHAT THE THING IS** (§24b).
**⚠ THE USER'S REPHRASING IS DATA.** "lower level textures disappear" and "+2 does not show the rock ledge of +1" describe the same screen but different mechanisms.
**⚠ A DIRECTIONAL WORD IN A REPORT IS A GRADIENT, AND GRADIENTS COME FROM KERNELS.** "fades INWARD instead of OUTWARD" says a weighted average is being fed the wrong samples.
**⚠ TWO SYMPTOMS REPORTED IN ONE BREATH ARE PROBABLY ONE BUG** (§25). **Ask what single quantity both symptoms read.**
**⚠ A SCREENSHOT CARRIES TERRAIN IDENTITY IF YOU KNOW YOUR OWN DEFS.** Grey tiled floor = `AB_RoofSurface`; dark 2x2 = `AirMaskMat`. §24c: **shrunken sprites are a DEPTH READOUT** (a small tree said drop/slot = 2, picking the right emitter out of three). §27: **hard cell-aligned rectangles mean a per-cell alpha written without its neighbours' agreement** - vanilla layers never produce a square edge. §28: **a square surviving past a stylised outline is an opaque fill under transparent art.** §28b: **a saturated red/magenta rim tracing an outline is an uncovered ShadowMask, not a broken material.** §29: **a cell-aligned staircase of MISSING floor is a fade with nothing behind it.**
**⚠ CHECK THAT YOUR CONFIGURATION CAN EXPRESS THE DIFFERENCE BEFORE RUNNING THE EXPERIMENT.** #231's water report was clean and worthless; #248/#254's Flat tiles were the same mistake in map form; a one-stone map cannot show a queue inversion.
**⚠ A CENSUS BEATS A MAGNITUDE - AND I IGNORED MY OWN RULE.**
**⚠ n=2 IS NOT A PATTERN, AND NEITHER IS n=4.** Report the RANGE and stop naming drivers.
**⚠ TILE-INDEPENDENT WINS BEAT TILE-DEPENDENT ONES.** Rank by worst case across conditions.
**⚠ Measure the ratio before optimising the half you assumed - and RE-measure after.**

# 25. 🔧 FIXED (UNVERIFIED IN PLAY): ONE `ABSkySync` BUG, TWO PUBLISHED SYMPTOMS
**The trigger, shared.** `Building.SpawnSetup` calls `map.edificeGrid.Register(this)` **without consulting `respawningAfterLoad`**, so `ABSkySync.SyncAbove` re-derives the ENTIRE sky band on every load. Both symptoms are reload-only and both compound, because the rewritten terrain is then saved.
**(a) Fog blob - `AB_MountainTop` -> `AB_WallTop`.** `Resolve` tested *impassable edifice* before *natural roof*. Undug rock is an impassable edifice under a natural roof, so mass above unmined rock became `AB_WallTop`, which is `dontRender` and `ShowsBelow`-true: the mass turned see-through and `EmitBelowFogFan` painted the SURFACE's fog through it.
**(b) Doubled, inverted stairs - `AB_RoofSurface` -> `AB_OpenAir`.** `CarveLanding` writes the landing *after* `base.SpawnSetup` already ran the sync. `Resolve` sees an unroofed `Building_Door` (`PassThroughOnly`) and returns `AB_OpenAir`; the landing goes see-through and the level below's stairwell prints into it. Up-art and down-art are vertical mirrors.
**Fix, four parts.** (1) precedence is constructed roof -> **natural roof** -> impassable edifice -> open air; (2) `IsDerived` no longer contains `AB_MountainTop` - the rule is **one-way**; (3) `SyncAbove` bails on `CarriesOwnStructure` and on the solid -> air transition within a link's landing apron; (4) `RepairAfterLoad` from `ABBandMap.FinalizeInit`, **placed there because that is the first moment this load's damage has already happened**.
**⚠ THE REPAIR IS TWO NARROW TRANSITIONS, NOT A RE-DERIVE.** Both rules can only move a cell back to a state the generator itself produces. Idempotent; logs a count when it repairs anything.

# 27. ✅ FIXED AND VERIFIED: BELOW-SNOW FADED THE WRONG WAY AT ROCKY PEAKS
The layer resolved visibility for the CENTRE cell, then sampled the nine-neighbour kernel straight out of `SnowGrid` at `z - drop`. A neighbour under a rocky peak is opaque from above but its *lower-level* cell usually has snow, so the kernel read off-screen snow and held full opacity right up to the peak; the opaque cell writes alpha 0 across its own nine vertices, giving a square edge. **Fix:** a one-cell-apron visibility cache built once per Regenerate from the shared gate, and three sample classes where there were two - outside the playable band -> **centre depth** (vanilla's map-edge rule, band-local); inside but not visible -> **zero**; visible -> sample at the centre's drop. **361 gate calls over the apron instead of 289 plus eight per visible cell.**

# 28. ✅ FIXED AND VERIFIED: THE FILL SQUARED OFF THE SILHOUETTE, ONCE PER LEVEL
**Report:** "every layer creates a new layer on top. At the mountain edges we get both the stylized black border of mineable rock, and the square texture."
**Root cause.** Vanilla rock is ONLY its atlas tile, and that tile's TRANSPARENCY is load-bearing. An opaque full-cell fill underneath refills the rounded corners and wavy lip, so past the black border the cell squares off - once per level, because **three emitters** draw fill (§6a).
**Fix:** erode the fill to the same link rule the tile's mask uses, via `ABNineFan.CoverInterior` - the DUAL of `Cover` (dilation vs erosion). An all-linked cell yields a fully covered fan, geometrically the quad, **so mass interiors are byte-identical**. Each caller passes its OWN link rule's answers: the cap counts MEADOW as linked (its fill must not retract where the meadow fans own the transition), the cross-level emitter counts only mass. `FieldFadeClone` is kept separate from `FieldClone` so the cap's opaque quads cannot change shader as a side effect. `ABNineFan.AddFan` gained a per-vertex-colour core so the cliff ramp survives the fan's THREE vertex rows.

## 28b. ✅ FIXED: THE RED RIM WAS A HOLE, AND THE OUTCROPS WERE A REUSED PREDICATE
1. **Outcrops kept their square.** `PrintBelowTerrain` gated erosion on `massCell`, the DECORATION gate, which carries `drop > slot` - a condition that exists so two emitters do not double-draw at one level down, and nothing to do with the fill. An undug rock outcrop exactly one level below therefore kept its hard quad under its own transparent sprite. Replaced by `TryMassFillCoverage`, which picks the rule by who draws the outline: a **rock edifice** brings its own sprite and links with rock and the MAP EDGE but never soil (mass rule); sky mass and deep mined floors are decorated by our atlas tile (cap rule). An **isolated** rock keeps its full quad - no linked cardinal means erosion would collapse to the centre vertex and ring it with a halo.
2. **The red rim was shader garbage, not a broken material.** The fill IS the backdrop - the viewing cell is `dontRender`, so vanilla emits only a ShadowMask - and eroding exposed it. It appeared only on unlinked faces, which is why it looked south/east-specific. **The competing theory (a shrunken sprite in a full-size cell) was killed by reading `ABDepthView.CanShrink`, which excludes rock by def.**

# 29. ✅ ACCEPTED ON LOOK (#260): THE DEPTH STACK
**Report:** "we are rendering the same rock type under the mineable and not sampling the stone underneath, so each tier looks as if it's laying on another. Additionally the effect works, but only one layer down, and it should cut through all layers."

**Two faults, one fix.** §28b's backdrop borrowed terrain from a LATERAL neighbour, so a mass cell was drawn against its own level's ground rather than the mountain continuing down. And `TryResolveVisibleBelow` stops at the first non-see-through cell, which a mass cell is, so a column resolved exactly ONE level.

**`BuildDepthStack`** walks one Slot at a time from the first visible cell, re-entering the shared descent whenever it lands on see-through terrain (so an air gap is crossed exactly as the normal view crosses it), and stops on: a non-mass cell (**the solid floor, INCLUDED as the opaque bottom** - the user's chosen stopping rule), fog, the gutter, or the map floor. Levels draw **deepest first**, each with its own erosion.

**Two defects found in the first cut of this, both mine, both from asserting rather than measuring:**
- **Holes.** "The bottom never erodes, therefore the bottom is opaque" is a claim about intent, not about the mesh: `PrintBelowTerrain` draws NOTHING on a `dontRender` or material-less cell, so everything above eroded onto a hole - a cell-aligned staircase of missing floor. Now a `laidOpaque` flag is carried up the stack and erosion is permitted only once something opaque has actually been laid.
- **Queue inversion.** Only the deeper levels were re-queued, leaving the nearest on its natural queue - which inverts whenever the deep terrain out-ranks the near one (stone 190+ over soil), and only on maps with two or more stone types. **`DepthQueue` now re-queues EVERY level**, stride 32 with the material's own precedence as a 0-31 tiebreak inside its level, whole band inside the terrain family. Edge-fade fans are depth-queued with the fill they belong to. **A single-level column is left completely untouched** - ordering only matters within a column, so one-level columns are provably unchanged.

**⚠ COST NEVER MEASURED.** See §0.
